gen_risks.description: Climate-induced flooding, heavy precipitation, and extreme heat risk damaging bridges, link roads, and agricultural market assets, disrupting connectivity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient engineering parameters, cantilever abutments, scour protection, raised deck soffits, and 'Green Roads for Water' concepts into civil works.
gen_risks.evidence: The key climate and natural hazards present in Sierra Leone are flooding, landslides, extreme heat, and wildfire.

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability, high inflation, and severe fiscal stress risk delaying government counterpart funding and straining local construction capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure US$74 million IDA grant funding for baseline core investments and implement flexible disbursement arrangements to buffer fiscal pressures.
gen_risks.evidence: macroeconomic environment, which is characterized by intensified fiscal pressures, soaring inflation driven by global supply shocks, and a slowdown of trade activities.

gen_risks.description: Unfunded financial gap on ongoing SCADeP bridge contracts threatens completion of critical rural bridges if government funding fails to materialize.
gen_risks.mitigation: Reallocate US$4 million from project IDA grant resources under Subcomponent 2(b) after SCADeP funds are exhausted, contingent on formal government commitment.
gen_risks.evidence: The total cost of the four signed contracts is US$33.3 million against a total budget of US$26.2 million under SCADeP.

gen_risks.description: Institutional fragmentation and overlapping responsibilities across multiple transport and agricultural agencies risk causing coordination delays and implementation friction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a National Project Steering Committee (NPSC) for inter-agency alignment and assign technical Focal Points from SLRA and MAFS to support the PCIU.
gen_risks.evidence: The institutional framework for transport sector management in Sierra Leone is fragmented and lacks systematic coordination among the multiple agencies operating with overlapping responsibilities.

gen_risks.description: Low revenue collection by the Road Maintenance Fund Administration risks inadequate long-term maintenance of newly constructed roads and bridges.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Bridge and Road Asset Management Systems (BMS/RAMS) to prioritize maintenance budgets, and deliver technical assistance to optimize road fund sustainability.
gen_risks.evidence: In 2020, the RMFA collected approximately US$12.5 million equivalent... which is a small fraction of the actual support needed for road maintenance

gen_risks.description: High baseline financial management risk due to the implementing unit's limited prior experience with World Bank FM procedures and control weaknesses.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a dedicated FM Specialist and Internal Auditor, adopt an approved FM manual, procure accounting software, and conduct specialized FM training.
gen_risks.evidence: The FM risk before considering the mitigating measures is 'High' mainly due to: (i) Insufficient experience of MTA with the World Bank’s FM procedures

gen_risks.description: Substantial procurement capacity risks and delays due to lack of a pre-existing procurement unit within the Project Coordination and Implementation Unit.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated procurement function in PCIU staffed with qualified specialists, adopt STEP tracking, and implement the approved PPSD.
gen_risks.evidence: The PCIU does not have a procurement unit currently and it will be established and staffed with a qualified and experienced person

gen_risks.description: Risk of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) during civil works and public transport operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt and implement a project-specific SEA/SH Action Plan, establish confidential grievance channels, install CCTV/lighting, and conduct operator training.
gen_risks.evidence: the Recipient shall... adopt and disclose the Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment Action Plan consistent with the ESCP and relevant ESSs.

gen_risks.description: High baseline rate of road crash fatalities and lack of synchronized crash data threaten safety on urban and rural project corridors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement targeted corridor road safety spot improvements, install traffic signals and guardrails, and establish a national road safety database and guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: WHO estimates that Sierra Leone has 33 road crash fatalities per 100,000 population annually, recording the third highest road crash fatality rate

gen_risks.description: Gender and digital divide among rural farmers risk limiting access to and adoption of the upgraded Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS).
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop Integrated Voice Response (IVR) systems, partner with women's groups/NGOs for field outreach, and provide hands-on digital literacy training to rural users.
gen_risks.evidence: exclusive reliance on AMIS mobile apps for accessing data and information could indeed pose a barrier for rural women who have less access to smartphones

gen_risks.description: Resistance or friction during the formalization and fleet expansion of unregulated informal paratransit operators in Freetown.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a 'lease-operate-own' model engaging corporatized operator entities, provide professionalization training, and involve SLPTA in operator transition management.
gen_risks.evidence: Public transport services are experiencing a rapid growth of unregulated informal providers, operating minibuses, locally called poda-podas.

gen_risks.description: Legal covenant and effectiveness conditions regarding key staff recruitment, manual adoption, and account opening risk delaying project startup.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Project Preparation Advance (PPA) resources to advance procurement of key staff, PIM drafting, and fiduciary setup prior to grant effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient has: (i) established a procurement unit... and (ii) hired a financial management specialist, an internal auditor, and a social specialist

gen_risks.description: Potential physical or economic displacement resulting from civil works for bridge link roads and market facilities requiring land acquisition.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt, disclose, and implement updated Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) and maintain active community consultation and local grievance redress mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: the Recipient shall: (i) adopt and disclose... (iii) the updated Resettlement Action Plan for Component 2;

gen_risks.description: Limited technical and financial capacity within local councils and market committees to ensure long-term maintenance of constructed market infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver tailored training on revenue generation, fund management, and asset maintenance planning to local councils, market committees, and market queens.
gen_risks.evidence: local councils are responsible for the establishment and administration of market centers and related facilities per the Local Government Act 2022.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance is rated Substantial. This project's activities are not highly sensitive to moderate perturbations in the political dispensation, although pronounced degeneration in political stability could still undermine their implementation. The more likely risk is that poor governance may affect implementation for the road sector, resulting in reduced commitment during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through close supervision, strict adherence to the criteria for beneficiary selection, and fiduciary oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed as Substantial. Sierra Leone's post-pandemic recovery was disrupted by concurrent domestic and external shocks. Inflation and exchange rate depreciation reached record levels, depressing economic activity and triggering a severe cost-of-living crisis. Fiscal accounts have deteriorated on account of macroeconomic headwinds and policy slippages, and risks to debt sustainability have intensified. The economy is projected to grow at 3.8 percent on average during 2023-2025, below the long-term trend, and this baseline is vulnerable to downside risks given recent fiscal slippages and expenditure overruns. The macroeconomic risk may raise concerns about contractors' cost overrun and delay of payment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Key macroeconomic reforms will help reduce the imbalances and avoid the downside risks. The project is 100 percent financed by IDA which will help mitigate the macroeconomic challenges to project implementation.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. The key fiduciary risks are related to the overall governance context of the project, the risk that procurement of project works may be delayed and/or result in higher-than-expected bid prices or poorly performing contractors, and difficulty retaining qualified procurement and FM professionals in the PCIU.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated by implementing an action plan that aims to strengthen the accountability and control framework for project implementation and improve overall fiduciary performance, and by ensuring adequate procurement and FM training. The PPSD will establish appropriate prequalification requirements and adopt standard lessons from experience procuring similar works contracts in Sierra Leone. The FM risk will be further mitigated by recruiting an internal auditor under PCIU.

gt_risks.description: The project's E&S risk is Substantial (para 74, explicitly pointing to section V.D for detail - para 74 states both environment risk and social risk are rated Substantial 'as indicated in section V.D'). Section V.D (paras 64-68): overall E&S risk classification is Substantial, with eight of ten Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) applying. Environmental risk is Substantial: construction activities are expected to generate air/noise nuisance, construction waste, and traffic/worker safety issues, and Component 2 in particular could affect downstream water users (water quality/hydrology, navigation, fish catch, riparian vegetation), with some impacts potentially long-term or irreversible (e.g. accidental spill of used oil/electrolytes/hazardous materials into the river during construction). Social risk is also Substantial: key risks include physical and economic displacement of boat/ferry operators, loaders, and traders after bridge construction; SEA/SH risks from the contractor workforce; elite capture in market-infrastructure interventions; social exclusion of vulnerable groups (persons with disabilities, women/small traders, the landless, elders); and secondary risks including potential child labor, communicable-disease spread from the contractor workforce, and local conflict over benefit-sharing from downstream impacts.
gt_risks.mitigation: Standard measures per the ESIA/ESMP to be prepared for project activities, including energy-efficiency measures per World Bank EHS Guidelines/GIIPs; a site-specific SEA/SH risk assessment and commensurate GBV/SEA/SH action plan; the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) and Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), disclosed April 19, 2024; hiring a social specialist with GBV/SEA/SH experience before project effectiveness; an ESIA and Resettlement Action Plan/livelihoods restoration plan already under development for the seven originally-planned bridges, with updated ESIA/ESMP/RAP and a SEA/SH action plan to be disclosed within one month of effectiveness; and a functional grievance mechanism (GM) plus Labor Management Procedures (LMP) for project workers.
